A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stiefel Flow Matching study. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–6, Figures 1–11, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QM9 and GEOM evaluations in Tables 1–2, ablations and timing measurements in Tables 5–6, and empirical logarithm-convergence analysis in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, timing measurements, and empirical logarithm analysis, including their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–D retain the same manifold formulation, architecture, flow-matching objective, approximate equivariant optimal transport, and sampling algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 and GEOM-Drugs for structure elucidation from molecular formula and moments of inertia. No datasets, tasks, or evaluated scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator membership: Stiefel Random, KREED, KREED-XL, and KREED-XL-proj, with KREED-XL-DPS additionally evaluated on QM9. The added software citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain identical splits, preprocessing, metrics, model sizes, training budgets, and sampling procedures, including the GEOM procedure that generates 30 samples and retains up to 10 valid samples.

E4.justification: The optimal-transport, stochasticity, and timestep-sampling ablations in Table 5 are unchanged, as are the molecular examples, trajectory analyses, and Appendix E logarithm-convergence study.

E5.justification: Both versions define error bars as standard errors of the mean and use the same uncertainty reporting in Tables 1, 2, and 5. No run counts, seed information, or statistical testing are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative findings match, including the appendix results. At RMSD below 0.25 Å, QM9 Stiefel FM success remains 15.17 ± 0.31%, and GEOM Stiefel FM-OT (filter) remains 3.94 ± 0.11%.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and Appendix B theorems and proofs are unchanged. The citation suffix adjustment in Appendix B.2 does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning exact moment constraints, equivariant optimal transport, and success rates and computational cost relative to Euclidean diffusion.

C2.justification: Interpretations of GEOM underfitting, validity filtering, and optimal transport remain unchanged. The limitations concerning molecular-formula input, planar molecules, and experimental rotational constants are also retained in Section 6.1 and Appendix A.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies py3Dmol as the molecular visualization tool and acknowledges software including PyTorch Lightning, Geomstats, einops, pybind11, and Eigen. This adds implementation provenance; the technical procedures, hyperparameters, hardware, timings, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting its software acknowledgments, including PyTorch, Geomstats, py3Dmol, NumPy, and SciPy. Section 5 and the positioning against prior scientific work remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a visualization-credit sentence and a software acknowledgment paragraph, updates the publication header, and adjusts citation disambiguation. The main narrative and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to the ICLR 2025 publication notice, and expanded acknowledgments and references reflow those pages. All figures, tables, captions, and their arrangements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides fuller software attribution, but the substantive main text and appendices retain identical methods, proofs, experiments, interpretations, and limitations. The added credits offer limited provenance information without materially changing reproducibility guidance or scientific support, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
